summary: Round 1 (new module). The one MARK (`produit_projectif`, every p = q + 1, arbitrary dimensions n i, Hausdorff σ-compact factors, dimension Σ n i + q) is earned: σ-compact ⇔ second countable for Hausdorff locally Euclidean spaces, so it is exactly the « variété » reading, and the induction from the two-factor case through `homeomorphInsertNth` and transport along a homeomorphism is sound. The three partial rows are correctly partial. THE FINDING on Prop. 2's proof is right and fair: scan p. 244 prints the lift « systèmes de p nombres réels positifs dont le produit est égal à 1 … définit un automorphisme de la structure conique affine du produit » with no dimension restriction anywhere in Déf. 1/Prop. 2 (Theorem A and the corollary use factors of different dimensions); in product cone charts (λᵢ) is diag(λᵢ I_{dim F(Bᵢ)}), the conical group is GU = {|det| = 1}, so the element is conical iff ∏ λᵢ^{dim F(Bᵢ)} = 1 — `det_eq_one_of_isGXMorphism_blockHom` (both directions with `isGXMorphism_blockHom`) and `not_isGXMorphism_blockHom_of_ne` ((2, 1/2) for a ≠ b) prove it; no other normalisation is available (the homotheties of F(Bᵢ) are Déf. 3's, fixed). Prop. 2's STATEMENT survives (the error is in an « On peut encore remarquer » side remark): the corrected lift `torusPair` (λ₁^{a+1} λ₂^{b+1} = 1, λ₂/λ₁ = μ) gives the torus action, free, with orbits the fibres. One minor: Déf. 1's own content (the ℝ₊*² principal-bundle structure on F(B₁) × F(B₂)) is not formalized even for p = 2, which the REPORT does not say. Scoped ProdCone instances verified inactive outside the scope; kb/0002 clean. Ready to graduate.

checks.finding_check: Scan p. 244 (PDF p. 17), read as an image: « On peut encore remarquer que R^{+p}/R^+ se relève suivant le sous-groupe de R^{+p} formé des systèmes de p nombres réels positifs dont le produit est égal à 1. Un élément de ce sous-groupe définit un automorphisme de la structure conique affine du produit des F(B_i) qui se projette donc suivant un automorphisme projectif de la structure de la base » — as transcribed (l.750–755, no final period). Neither Déf. 1, Prop. 2 nor the proof restricts the dimensions, and the corollary / Theorem A explicitly use arbitrary dims. Lean: `det_eq_one_of_isGXMorphism_blockHom` [Nonempty V] [Nonempty W]: if blockHom c₁ c₂ is a GU-morphism of the product then c₁^{a+1} c₂^{b+1} = 1 (rigidity: the GU element agreeing with diag(c₁, c₂) on an open set equals it, `eq_of_eqOn`); `isGXMorphism_blockHom` is the converse; `not_isGXMorphism_blockHom_of_ne` (a ≠ b): (2, 1/2) has product 1 and is not conical (2^{a+1} = 2^{b+1} forces a = b). Nonemptiness is needed and natural (an empty product makes every map a morphism). GU is {|det| = 1} (`mem_GU`, the p. 236 i(ḡ) = |det g|^{-1/n} g), so no rescaling of the factors' homotheties can make the printed subgroup conical: Benzécri's lift is right exactly when all F(Bᵢ) have the same dimension. Fair reading. The statement of Prop. 2 is TRUE: ℝ^{+p}/ℝ^+ lifts to {∏ λᵢ^{dim F(Bᵢ)} = 1} (a complement of the diagonal, since the diagonal λ has ∏ = λ^{Σ dim F(Bᵢ)}), and in any case every (λᵢ) ∈ ℝ^{+p} is a GL-map commuting with the diagonal and descends to a projective automorphism of the base — the last printed sentence (« Un élément quelconque de R^{+p} est seulement un automorphisme affin ») is consistent with that. Exponent convention: the REPORT's « ∏ λᵢ^{nᵢ} » means nᵢ = dim F(Bᵢ) = dim Bᵢ + 1 (a + 1, b + 1 in Lean), which it does not say (nit)

general_p: Recommendation for Déf. 1 / Props. 2–3 at every p. The corollary's induction works because its conclusion is about plain topological spaces and transports along a homeomorphism; Props. 2–3 are about F⁻¹ of a product CONE, so the same induction needs a conical identification at each step. (a) Prop. 3 IS reachable by induction: with Wₖ := F(B₂) × … × F(B_p) built by nested binary ProdCone products, F⁻¹(F(B₁) × W) ≅ F⁻¹(F(B₁) × F(F⁻¹ W)) as locally projective manifolds by the § 2 unit (`ConeBase.unitMap` with `unitMap_bijective`, `isGXMorphism_unitMap`, which need neither a Hausdorff base nor connectedness, WP-45r AUDIT-1) and `isGXMorphism_prodMap`; then binary Prop. 3 applies to (B₁, F⁻¹ W), given three small lemmas: homogeneity / sweepability / divisibility are invariant under a projective isomorphism; F⁻¹ W is Hausdorff and paracompact (σ-compact) — it is ≃ₜ B₂ × … × B_p × ℝ₊*^{p−2} by iterating exists_prodBase_homeomorph; and the nested product is conically isomorphic to the flat one (a block permutation, |det| = 1). (b) Déf. 1 and Prop. 2 are better done FLAT, not by induction: the nested route yields an iterated ℝ₊* action, not ℝ^{+p}/ℝ^+ acting at once with the product-1 normalisation the statement is about. Generalise blockEquiv/blockGL/blockGU from Fin (a+1) ⊕ Fin (b+1) to Σ i, Fin (nᵢ+1) (Fin.sigma-type equivalence + LinearEquiv.piCongr / Matrix.blockDiagonal'-style det product), blockPt to ∀ i, RnO (nᵢ+1), and torusPair to the complement {∏ λᵢ^{nᵢ+1} = 1}; every binary proof in the file is already coordinatewise and transfers. Estimated: Déf. 1 + Prop. 2 flat ≈ the size of the current BlockHom section; Prop. 3 by (a) ≈ 150 lines plus the three invariance lemmas
fidelity_summary: The corollary of Prop. 3 is the printed statement for every p with « variété » = Hausdorff + σ-compact (⇔ second countable); MARK earned. Déf. 1 (the product cone, p = 2, any two cones), Prop. 2 (p = 2, torus action free with orbits the fibres; principal-bundle triviality for paracompact factors) and Prop. 3 (p = 2, all three cases) are faithful and correctly partial. The finding is fair: Benzécri's product-1 lift is conical iff all factors have the same dimension; the corrected lift is ∏ λᵢ^{dim F(Bᵢ)} = 1, and Prop. 2's statement is unaffected. Graduation: ready; minor 1 is an additional disclosure (or five short lemmas).
